title: Microsoft 365 admin center: rules that automate agent lifecycle management
summary: The documented lifecycle rules, admin paths, licensing and preview Graph operations support the briefing. The pre-check's two label warnings are cosmetic: Microsoft documents both Block and Unblock, and both Publish to store and Reject submission. One minor checklist-to-table omission remains.

claims.claim: Reassignment transfers ownership to the previous owner's manager using the Microsoft Entra hierarchy.

claims.claim: Apply template is a one-time bulk operation rather than a scheduled rule.
claims.quote: The Apply template action is a one-time bulk operation. It isn't a scheduled rule.

claims.claim: The Agent settings page does not document a separate rule for deleting inactive agents.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "delete"; opened Agent settings and Agent actions. Settings lists five bulk actions, none deleting inactive agents; actions documents manual deletion and automatic permanent deletion after soft-delete retention.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: The settings page does not specify a risky-agent rule condition or which risk signals a rule consumes.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "risky" "conditions"; read Agent settings, Agent 365 overview, registry risk sections and detect-risky-agents. No passage specifies a risky-agent condition or a mapping of risk signals into management rules.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 overview describes rules-based lifecycle management that can block risky agents.
claims.quote: Leverage rules-based agent management to automatically enforce lifecycle policies, such as flagging ownerless agents, or blocking risky agents.

claims.claim: Registry manual actions include installation, blocking, unblocking, uninstallation and pinning, subject to eligibility.
claims.quote: Install and uninstall; Block and unblock. For information about actions related to the agent registry list, such as Export to Excel, Upload custom agent, and Manage pinned agents, see Agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Only agents deployed to some or all users can be pinned.
claims.quote: You can only pin agents that are deployed to some or all users.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder agents affects availability in Copilot and other hosts such as Outlook and Teams.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking Copilot Studio agents affects availability in Copilot and other hosts such as Outlook and Teams.
claims.quote: It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams, or other Microsoft 365 applications.

claims.claim: Blocking a SharePoint agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Blocking a Foundry agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Researcher can be blocked tenant-wide but its Edit users panel is disabled.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the Edit users panel is disabled. To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the Block action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Analyst can be blocked tenant-wide but its Edit users panel is disabled.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the Edit users panel is disabled. To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the Block action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Agents can become ownerless when their creator leaves, and All agents has an Agents without owners card.
claims.quote: Shared agents can become ownerless when you delete the user who created them from the organization. When you select the Agents without owners card, the agent list is filtered to show the agents based on Publisher type and Owner.

claims.claim: Viewing registry risk signals requires an E7 or A365 tenant licence.
claims.quote: Prerequisites for viewing risk signals: Your tenant must have an E7 or A365 license.

claims.claim: Registry risk signals can come from Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender.
claims.quote: Displays the Microsoft security platforms contributing risk signals for the agent, such as Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Defender. Only platforms with contributing signals are shown.

claims.claim: Deletion in the Microsoft 365 admin center is soft deletion.
claims.quote: When you delete an agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the agent is soft deleted.

claims.claim: Soft-deleted agents have a 30-day recovery window.
claims.quote: During the 30-day retention period, you can restore the agent or permanently delete it.

claims.claim: Permanent deletion cannot be undone.
claims.quote: Permanently deleting an agent removes the agent and its associated resources and can't be undone.

claims.claim: The settings page does not describe notification options for affected users and owners when these rules act.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "notifications"; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365 "rules" "notifications". Read Agent settings and Notify agents lifecycle-event excerpt; the latter concerns developer handlers, not rule notifications to users or owners.

claims.claim: Manual blocking and unblocking are at Agents > All agents > agent > Block / Unblock.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject rejects a pending package title submission.

claims.claim: The rejection request should supply the matching staged version.
claims.quote: The schema defines both parameters as optional. This doesn't mean that omitting version selects the latest or pending version. Supply the version of the staged submission you're rejecting.

claims.claim: Sharing limits can govern agents built in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: You can control and limit how Copilot Studio agents are shared by applying the Editor and Viewer permission assignments to individuals who need to access Copilot Studio, and then configuring the permissions for who can share with whom.

claims.quote: You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Sharing limits apply only to agents requiring authentication.
claims.quote: Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.

claims.claim: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share.
claims.quote: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share an app, flow, or agent.

claims.claim: Sharing-rule enforcement does not affect users who already had access before the rules were applied.
claims.quote: This enforcement doesn't affect users who already have access to the app, flow, or agent before you apply the rules.

claims.claim: Whether lifecycle rules can be scoped by environment, publisher or tag remains unspecified in the checked documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "publisher" "environment" "tag". Read Agent settings, Copilot controls for management and registry documentation. Settings says to define applicable criteria but doesn't identify those three dimensions as rule criteria.

claims.claim: Lifecycle rules are admin-opt-in: administrators create and run rules rather than receiving default enforcement.
claims.quote: go to Agents > Settings > Agent management rules, and then select Add rule. In the rule details pane, choose all agents or select a subset of agents from the list. Run the rule to apply the template.

claims.fix: The checklist step 'Check manager attributes in Entra for the maker population of Agent Builder agents so reassignment works' has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the existing explanation that reassignment depends on accurate manager data.

claims.claim: The lifecycle-rule capability is included in existing Microsoft 365 licensing, supporting cost none for the feature itself.

claims.quote: The new owner gets full edit and delete permissions, plus access to any files the previous owner uploaded.
